nodes.name: PAN flower-like polymerization
nodes.procedure: 50 ml of acrylonitrile (AN) and 50 mg of azobisisobutyronitrile (AIBN) were combined with 50 mL of acetone (ACE) solvent to prepare polyacrylonitrile (PAN) flower-like polymer superstructures. The reaction was conducted at 70 °C for 2 h in a tightly sealed glass vial to ensure an oxygen-free environment, utilizing an oil bath and nitrogen (N2) gas protection, without stirring, which is critical for the polymerization process. The resulting white product was dried overnight at room temperature in a vacuum oven to remove any unreacted monomer and solvent, which exhibited a distinct flower-like morphology.

nodes.name: CNF stabilization and carbonization
nodes.procedure: The as-prepared PAN flower-like superstructures were subjected to a thermal stabilization process in the air to enhance their structural integrity prior to carbonization. Specifically, the samples were heated to 230 °C in an air atmosphere for 2 h, with a slow ramping rate of 0.2 °C/min. Following the stabilization process, the stabilized PAN particles were subsequently carbonized at 900 °C in an N2 atmosphere to prepare carbon nanoflowers (CNF).

nodes.name: S-doped CNF preparation
nodes.procedure: 50 mg of 2,2'-bithienyl was first dissolved in 10 mL of methanol. Subsequently, 150 mg of CNF matrix was dispersed into the solution and the mixture was vigorously stirred for 1 h to ensure homogeneous impregnation. The resulting suspension was then transferred to an oven and dried at 60 °C to remove the solvent completely. Finally, the dried composite was subjected to pyrolysis under an inert atmosphere at 800 °C for 1 h, yielding the S-doped CNF matrix through thermal decomposition and carbonization processes.
nodes.source_text: Note 4. Synthesis of Os-SA@SNC sample (S-doping part)

nodes.name: Os-NP@NC impregnation and pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: 10 mL of osmium trichloride (OsCl3; 1 mg/mL) solution was slowly added into 150 mg CNF powder to prepare precursor. After stirring for 2 h, the solution was then placed in an oven to dry at 60 °C. Subsequently, the dried black powders were pyrolyzed in a furnace at 950 °C to synthesize the N-doped carbon supported Os nanocrystals sample (Os-NP@NC).

nodes.name: Os-SA@SNC impregnation and pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: 10 mL of OsCl3 solution was slowly added into S-doped CNF powder to prepare precursor. After stirring for 2 h, the solution was then placed in an oven to dry. Subsequently, the dried material was pyrolyzed in a furnace at 950 °C to synthesize the atomically dispersed Os-SA@SNC sample.
nodes.source_text: Note 4. Synthesis of Os-SA@SNC sample (Os loading part)

nodes.name: Os-SA@NC synthesis
nodes.procedure: 1 mL of OsCl3 solution was slowly added into 300 mg CNF powder, and then the mixture was stirred for 2 h, after that, the solution was placed in an oven to dry. Subsequently, the dried black powders were pyrolyzed in a furnace at 950 °C to synthesize the atomically dispersed Os-SA@NC sample.
